title: Calibration-led Quant Onboarding and Regression Ledger (rollback-safe)
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Build a reproducible, audit-friendly onboarding flow for quantization artifacts (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ) that attaches a time-stamped performance ledger and supports rollback-safe pinning. This ticket covers end-to-end automation: artifact ingestion, calibration-run harness, perf & quality baselines, publishing to the model catalog with immutable metadata, canary rollout gating, and longitudinal regression detection with automatic alerting and rollback playbook.
background: We currently accept quant artifacts ad-hoc and rely on manual perf notes in PRs. This leads to drift: different hardware/kernel combos, varying prompt mixes, and no centralized historical record for regressions. Customers pin quantized model versions but lack clear baselines to determine if a new quant profile degraded output quality or latency. Previous efforts (ENG-4721, ENG-9417) focused on CI gates and profile formats; this ticket creates a ledger and onboarding harness that ties artifact + runtime config to a verified perf snapshot and automated regression checks.
proposed_solution: 1) Artifact ingestion service: accept quant bundle + manifest (model version, quant type, quant seed, quant tool/version, target hardware tags). 2) Calibration harness: run deterministic token-level warmups + standardized prompt suites (unit prompts, safety prompts, infilling, long-context) on target hardware profiles. 3) Baseline snapshot: capture latency (P50/P95), throughput, peak memory, token generation stability, and quality metrics (embedding similarity to float baseline, logprob delta on eval set, and targeted decoding regressions). 4) Ledger entry: store immutable record (artifact hash, manifest, hardware, kernel selection, perf snapshot, PR link, uploader). 5) Catalog publishing: tag artifact as CANARY/PRODUCTION and enable automated canary with abort/rollback triggers. 6) Regression detector: nightly re-eval and on-publish statistical checks (bootstrap with thresholds + signal thresholds for quality and latency), plus alerting to eng/PM/QA channels. 7) Rollback and pinning UI ops: console endpoints to pin model+quant artifact version and a one-click rollback to previous ledger entry.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact ingestion accepts bundles with manifest and returns a signed artifact ID
Calibration harness produces repeatable perf snapshots within noise bounds across 3 runs
Ledger entries are immutable and searchable by artifact ID, model version, quant type, and hardware tag
Publishing to catalog sets a CANARY tag and triggers canary runs with abort on threshold breaches
Regression detector raises alert if embedding-similarity drops by >2% absolute OR latency P95 increases by >15% for production-tagged artifacts
Console shows timeline view of ledger entries and allows pinning/rollback to a prior artifact
tradeoffs: Tight thresholds reduce risk of regressions but increase false positives and onboarding friction
Extensive eval suites improve coverage but increase cost and wall-time for onboarding runs
Immutable ledger provides auditability at the cost of storage and ingestion complexity
Enforcing exact kernel/hardware matching for production gating simplifies reproducibility but reduces rollout flexibility for customers on different infrastructure

qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest schema validation and artifact-hash generation
Deterministic integration runs on internal small-GPU pool to verify noise bounds
Simulated regression pushes (synthetic perf degradations) to validate alerting and rollback behavior
Smoke tests for console pin/rollback and catalog visibility
Security review on artifact signing and access controls (simulate compromised bundle scenario)
notes_and_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created. Initial design doc linked. Assigned to Liam for implementation. Asha will own acceptance tests and QA runbook.

2026-03-11: Decided on artifact manifest fields: model_version, base_float_hash, quant_tool, quant_seed, hardware_tags, kernel_hint, training_meta. Action: add schema validation in ingest API (PR opened).

2026-03-12: Cal harness proto merged. Warmup strategy: deterministic prefix sequences + three independent runs; compute median metrics to reduce noisy aborts. Note: using embedding-similarity (cosine) against float baseline as primary quality signal.

2026-03-13: Telemetry mapping agreed with observability: p50/p95 latency, tokens_per_sec, peak_vram, embedding_cosine_median, logprob_mean_delta. Created dashboard panel IDs and Grafana alert thresholds for canary failure.

2026-03-14: First ingest test successful on internal awq-optimized artifact. Ledger entry created with artifact-id art_20260314_01. Found a small perf variance on A100 kernels; filing follow-up ENG-31247 to add kernel-tagging enforcement during canary.
2026-03-14: Review feedback from PM (Riley): add customer-impact tag and automated release notes generation for catalog entries. Added to acceptance criteria and implementation backlog.
rollback_playbook: Step 1: Auto-abort canary and mark artifact as CANARY_FAILED
Step 2: Create urgent issue with ledger diff between failed and last-green artifact
Step 3: Auto-schedule rollback to last-green artifact and notify on-call
Step 4: Run targeted regression tests against pinned artifact, escalate to model infra and quant authors
